package_info.why_malicious: The faker@6.6.6 package was intentionally sabotaged by its maintainer as a form of protestware. The maintainer removed all original source code, causing any installation of this version to break functionality for consumers. This deliberate disruption constitutes a denial-of-service attack on dependent projects, making the package malicious at the macro level.

execution_context.file_location: index.js (main entry point of the package)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
// All code removed intentionally by the maintainer
module.exports = () => { throw new Error('faker is no longer available'); };
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code immediately throws an error, preventing any use of the package and breaking dependent applications.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The package's main entry point is replaced with code that intentionally breaks all consumers by throwing an error on import.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A normal package should provide its advertised functionality. Instead, this version sabotages all usage.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: A package might throw an error if a critical dependency is missing or if the environment is unsupported, but not as a blanket denial of service.
key_indicators: Complete removal of all functional code

attack_chain.action: Maintainer publishes a new major version (6.6.6) with all source code removed and replaced by code that throws an error.
attack_chain.leads_to: Any project that upgrades to or installs faker@6.6.6 will immediately break at runtime.

attack_chain.action: Consumers of the package experience denial of service as their applications fail to start or run tests.
attack_chain.leads_to: Disruption of development pipelines and production systems relying on faker.

behavioral_signatures: Main entry point throws an error immediately on import
All functional code removed in a new major version
Sudden, unexplained breaking change in a widely used package
file_indicators: index.js or main file reduced to a single error-throwing statement
Absence of expected source files in the package
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for major version updates of critical dependencies that remove all or most source code, especially if the main entry point throws an error or otherwise disables functionality. Automated dependency analysis tools should flag packages where the main export is a function that only throws, or where the package contents are drastically reduced compared to previous versions. Review changelogs and diffs for sudden, unexplained code removal.
